tagline: The Healthy Way of Life Company
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the Hero because it reflects the company's ability to generate revenue per center efficiently, which is a key success factor in the fitness and wellness sector.

kpis.name: Average Revenue Per Center and Per Membership
kpis.explanation: Average annualized revenue generated per center and per membership
kpis.description: Average revenue per center and per membership is a key indicator of the company's financial performance and its ability to optimize memberships
kpis.signal: Significant increase in average revenue per center and per membership

kpis.name: Total Visits to Centers
kpis.explanation: Total number of annual visits to fitness centers
kpis.description: Total number of visits is an indicator of member engagement and center utilization
kpis.signal: Increased member engagement and center popularity

kpis.name: Total Center Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total annual revenue generated by fitness centers (memberships + in-center services)
kpis.description: Total center revenue includes membership fees and in-center service revenues
kpis.signal: Significant increase in total center revenue

kpis.name: Number of Operational Centers
kpis.explanation: Total number of operational fitness centers
kpis.description: Number of centers is a key indicator of network growth and expansion

kpis.name: Number of Individual Members
kpis.explanation: Total number of individual members enrolled (approximately 1.6 million members grouped into ~873k memberships)
kpis.description: Number of individual members is a key measure of customer base reach and growth

kpis.name: Average Annual Visits per Membership
kpis.explanation: Average number of annual visits per active membership
kpis.description: Average visits per membership is a key indicator of member engagement and center utilization
kpis.signal: Stable member engagement with frequent visits

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 5 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total Revenue of $2.995 billion in the most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net Income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 5 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net Income of $0.374 billion in the most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: Inability to attract and retain members and optimize memberships
risks.score_rationale: The company's success depends directly on its ability to attract and retain members and increase revenue per membership. Numerous factors could impact this critical capability including member engagement, pricing, consumer behavior, competition, economic conditions, and health threats.

risks.title: Increased competition and market share erosion
risks.score_rationale: Competitors are attempting to replicate the business model or offer similar services. Some competitors, particularly non-profit and government organizations, have cost advantages. Industry consolidation could intensify competition and limit the ability to attract members.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party suppliers
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on third-party suppliers for equipment and certain products and services. Any disruption to suppliers' operations or inability to identify alternative suppliers could impact center operations and brand expansion.

risks.title: Brand quality and reputation risks
risks.score_rationale: Life Time brand and reputation are among its most important assets. Any deterioration in brand quality or reputation would directly affect the ability to attract and retain members and could materially impact results.

risks.title: Macroeconomic risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to macroeconomic risks including tariffs, inflation, interest rates, taxes, and economic recessions, which could reduce discretionary spending and impact demand for premium services.

risks.title: Health and safety risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to public health risks such as pandemics and epidemics which could result in forced center closures and decreased member attendance.

risks.title: Growth and expansion risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is in a rapid growth phase with a plan to expand to 12-14 new centers per year and new business models (Life Time Work, Life Time Living). This rapid growth presents management and integration risks.

risks.title: Regulatory risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to changes in laws and regulations, particularly regarding taxes, labor, and business practices, which could increase operating costs.

ai_positioning.summary: Life Time actively integrates AI into its digital strategy. The company invests in its digital capabilities, including LAIC (Life Time AI Companion), its first generative AI-driven healthy way of life personal companion offering personalized content and recommendations to members. This initiative supports Life Time's omni-channel relationship with its members and expands its reach beyond physical centers.
evidence: Continuing to invest in our digital capabilities, including artificial intelligence such as LAIC, our first generative artificial intelligence driven healthy way of life personal companion with personalized content and recommendations, to strengthen our relationships with our members, reach more people looking for a Healthy Way of Life and more comprehensively address their health, fitness and wellness needs so that they can engage and connect with Life Time at any time or place.
